design_decisions.question: Merge where-clause predicates into the existing per-parameter generics entries, or append them as separate entries?
design_decisions.decision: Appended as separate, distinct entries (e.g. ["T", "where T : Clone"]). A predicate's own token-stream rendering does not, by itself, say which earlier type parameter it constrains (and WherePredicate is #[non_exhaustive], so exhaustively matching its internal shape to attribute it precisely would be fragile); keeping predicates as their own entries records the real information present (the predicate exists, verbatim) without fabricating an association the renderer cannot safely derive.

design_decisions.question: For an enum struct-variant's named field, scope the new Symbol at the enum level (matching the pre-existing, already-tested TypeIdentity scope for the same field) or at a new per-variant scope?
design_decisions.decision: Per-variant scope (`nested_scope(&nested, &variant_name)`), left the pre-existing field TypeIdentity scope untouched at the enum level to avoid breaking the already-passing `enum_variants_and_payload_types_are_observed` test (which asserts an exact scope-path match). Two different variants of the same enum can legitimately declare a field with the same name (`Active { id: u64 }` / `Inactive { id: u64 }`); scoping the new Symbol at the enum level would have silently collided them onto one identity from the moment it was introduced, which the existing (unrelated, untouched) TypeIdentity scoping already risks but this fix does not need to inherit or extend.

design_decisions.question: For a trait's associated const/type with no default value, does the fix still have a concrete Type to name?
design_decisions.decision: For an associated const, yes always -- `const NAME: Type;` requires a declared Type with no default needed, so a TypeIdentity is emitted unconditionally. For an associated type, no -- `type Foo;` (no default) declares only bounds, never a concrete Type node; emitting a TypeIdentity there would fabricate a type that is not actually spelled out in the declaration, so only a Symbol (role=Declaration) is emitted for that case, mirroring this module's established 'never fabricate compiler-resolved or absent information' doctrine used throughout every other extraction dimension this session.
